title: Northern Lights spotted across NI as sightings could continue for days
excerpt: The natural phenomenon is caused by increased solar activity
content:
Residents across Northern Ireland were left stunned as the sky was illuminated by the bright colours of the Northern Lights this weekend.

There were sightings of the natural phenomenon, known as the Aurora Borealis, on Saturday night, October 10, across parts of Co Antrim, Co Down, Co Armagh and Co Tyrone before being obscured by some cloud cover as the night went on.

The phenomenon is caused by increased solar activity, and is usually mostly visible near the Arctic Circle and northern Scotland. However, particularly strong activity levels meant they could be seen throughout much of the UK this weekend.

The Met Office has said sightings could continue to be possible during clear skies until Tuesday.

Northern Lights are caused by powerful solar eruptions from the Sun, called coronal mass ejections (CMEs). At the end of last week, the Sun unleashed CMEs directed towards the Earth.

This stream of charged particles can be captured by the Earth's magnetic field and directed to our atmosphere, especially towards polar regions. It is when the particles collide with oxygen and nitrogen the aurora lights are emitted.

The chances of seeing the phenomenon varies across the UK depending on its strength, as when activity levels reach reach 200nT (nanotesla) it can be visible in northern regions, but not further south.

However, on Saturday night, the levels reached around 600nT, increasing how far the Northern Lights were visible across the UK.
